record.title: Air Security reports a Solana starter repository used to deliver a remote-access payload through coding-agent workflows
record.summary: Air Security Research Lab’s 29 October report describes a GitHub repository posing as a Solana starter kit whose README instructed users to run a PowerShell command that downloaded and executed code. The report says its recovered archived payload installed a configured NetSupport remote-access client with hidden operation and login persistence. Air Security reports that the original payload endpoint was offline when checked and the named repository was later unavailable. The report documents a plausible agent-mediated delivery route, but does not establish that a coding agent executed the command, identify victims, or measure campaign prevalence. the research desk did not independently inspect or run the sample.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Air Security Research Lab published a report about the SolanaCry campaign on 29 October 2026.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Air Security says a GitHub repository presenting itself as a Solana starter kit contained a README command that downloaded and executed a PowerShell payload, in a workflow it says was intended to attract coding agents searching for a starter kit.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Air Security reports that an archived sample unpacked signed NetSupport components, configured remote access, hid user-facing controls and established login persistence; the research desk did not independently inspect or execute the sample.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The report does not establish that an AI coding agent executed the command, that a victim was infected through an agent, how many victims existed, or whether the infrastructure remains active.

evidence_gaps.description: The named GitHub repository is unavailable in the checked surface, so its original README and history were not independently inspected by the research desk.
The reported archived payload, its hash and described NetSupport configuration were not independently analyzed by the research desk or corroborated by another technical analyst in this review.
The report provides no victim count, confirmed agent executions, prevalence estimate or evidence of current active infrastructure.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported route is accurate, a repository selected through a coding-agent workflow exposed a Windows host to a remotely controlled client, a notable concrete risk for agent browsing and command execution. The score is limited by the single vendor report, unavailable repository and payload endpoint, unknown victim count, and lack of independent sample validation.
limitations: The source is a security vendor’s report and its author has a commercial interest in agent filtering products.
the research desk did not independently retrieve or execute the malware sample; reported mechanics remain CLAIMED.
The report says the original payload endpoint was offline; the repository was unavailable in a prior direct check.
No victim count, successful AI-agent execution, prevalence or current campaign activity was established.

Air Security reports that the original payload endpoint was offline when checked and the named repository was later unavailable. technical.claimed_result: Air Security reports that the repository and archived payload formed a malware delivery path aimed at developers using web-browsing coding agents.
technical.demonstrated_result: The vendor report was published and the public report describes its sample-analysis methods and claims. the research desk has not independently established the infection or agent-execution path.
technical.implementation_status: The named GitHub repository and original payload URL were unavailable at the time reported; the current status of the operator and infrastructure is unknown.
technical.mechanism: The report describes a Windows PowerShell command in a project README that fetched and executed remote code; it says the archived dropper installed a configured NetSupport client with hidden operation and login persistence.
technical.novelty: A vendor-reported example of an established remote-access malware delivery pattern adapted to repository selection and setup by AI coding agents. The agent-mediated portion is not independently verified.
technical.regime: Windows systems where a coding agent can browse project repositories and execute PowerShell setup commands; the specific lure presented as a Solana starter kit.
technical.reproducibility: No sample was retrieved, executed or independently analyzed by the research desk. The report provides a sample SHA-256 and describes archive recovery, enabling a future independent static-analysis check.
technical.strongest_baseline: Air Security’s report cites an earlier NetSupport campaign using a similar PowerShell delivery pattern; that comparison supports the vendor’s lineage hypothesis but does not establish agent-mediated infection in this case.

brief.title: Air Security reports a Solana starter repository used to deliver a remote-access payload through coding-agent workflows
brief.why_it_matters: Coding agents that search repositories and execute setup commands can turn malicious project documentation into a software supply-chain entry point. The report is a specific warning case, but its agent-selection and infection pathway remain vendor-reported rather than independently established.
